subject: Dynamic occupancy model with spatial random effect (dcar_normal)

messages.author: 2504f1f1633f946f
messages.subject: Dynamic occupancy model with spatial random effect (dcar_normal)
parts:
Hello, 
I was analyzing presence/absence data of amphibians with a dynamic occupancy model in JAGS. I followed: Royle, J. A., and Kéry, M. (2007). A Bayesian state-space formulation of dynamic occupancy models. Ecology 88, 1813–1823. doi:10.1890/06-0669.1
To this model, I added covariates for both the "observational submodel" and the "ecological submodel" with some variables related to initial occupancy, survival probabilty, and colonization probability. The model worked fine in JAGS.

Then, I discovered nimble, which allows to embed spatial random effects with the dcar_normal() function (and also seems to be much faster, up to 7 times faster than JAGS!).

So, I modified my JAGS code to include it in the nimbleCode() function, and then added the spatial random effect.

The models seems to run, however all the posterior of chain1 seems to be stucked to the initial value. Additionally, some to all posteriors in other chains seems to suffer the same issue.
Could you help me to figure out what is the problem?

I prepared two versions of my model: a full model, including all the variables I'm interested in, and a reduced model, including only one independent variable related to initial occupancy, colonization, and survival.
Both models include four varibles in the "observational submodel" (day, day^2, hour, hour^2)

Here is the code to run the models.
Furthermore, I will attach the scripts for the two models.

Since the dataset is still not published, if anyone wants to help, I will share the data privately.

All the best, 
Mattia

Code:


setwd("")


library(nimble)


# load the model
source("nimble_model - full.R")
source("nimble_model - reduced.R")


# load the data
load("data.Rdata")
load("neighborhood.Rdata")


# Bundle data
win.data <- list(y = y)
constants <- list(nsite = dim(y)[1], nrep = dim(y)[2], nyear = dim(y)[3],
                  day = tab_day, hour = tab_hour,
                  wood = wood, area = area, perm = perm, PC = PC, PCinc = PCinc, SPinc = SPinc,
                  adj = adiacenti,num_adj = num_adiacenti, sumneigh = sumneigh, weights = rep(1,sumneigh))


#####
# REDUCED MODEL
#####


# parameters to monitor
params<-c("psi1_int","psi1_wood",
          "phi_int","phi_wood",
          "gamma_int","gamma_wood",
          "z","p_int","p_day1","p_day2","p_hour1","p_hour2",
          "psi1_rho","phi_rho","gamma_rho","psi1_tau","phi_tau","gamma_tau")


# inits
initsFunction <- function() list(psi1_int = rnorm(1,0,10), psi1_wood = rnorm(1,0,10),  
                                 phi_int = rnorm(1,0,10), phi_wood = rnorm(1,0,10),
                                 gamma_int = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_wood = rnorm(1,0,10),
                                 p_int = rnorm(1,0,10), p_day1 = rnorm(1,0,10), p_day2 = rnorm(1,0,10), p_hour1 = rnorm(1,0,10), p_hour2 = rnorm(1,0,10))


# MCMC settings
ni <- 2000
nb <- ni*1/2
nt <- 1
nc <- 3


# Run the model
start.time <- Sys.time()
out <- nimbleMCMC(code = multiseason_nimble_car_reduced, constants = constants,
                       data = win.data, inits = initsFunction,
                       nchains = 3, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, thin = nt,
                       #summary = TRUE, # WAIC = TRUE,
                       monitors = params)
Sys.time()-start.time


# SUMMARY
parms<-c("psi1_int","psi1_wood",
          "phi_int","phi_wood",
          "gamma_int","gamma_wood",
          "p_int","p_day1","p_day2","p_hour1","p_hour2")


summary(out$chain1[,colnames(out$chain1)%in%parms])
summary(out$chain2[,colnames(out$chain2)%in%parms])
summary(out$chain3[,colnames(out$chain3)%in%parms])




#####
# FULL MODEL
#####


# parameters to monitor
params<-c("psi1_int","psi1_fish","psi1_perm","psi1_area","psi1_wood",
          "phi_int","phi_fish","phi_PC","phi_perm","phi_area","phi_wood",
          "gamma_int","gamma_fish","gamma_PC","gamma_perm","gamma_area","gamma_wood","gamma_PCinc","gamma_SPinc",
          "z","p_int","p_day1","p_day2","p_hour1","p_hour2",
          "psi1_rho","phi_rho","gamma_rho","psi1_tau","phi_tau","gamma_tau")


# inits
initsFunction <- function() list(psi1_int = rnorm(1,0,10), psi1_wood = rnorm(1,0,10), psi1_fish = rnorm(1,0,10), psi1_perm = rnorm(1,0,10), psi1_area = rnorm(1,0,10),
                                 phi_int = rnorm(1,0,10), phi_wood = rnorm(1,0,10), phi_fish = rnorm(1,0,10), phi_perm = rnorm(1,0,10), phi_area = rnorm(1,0,10), phi_PC = rnorm(1,0,10),
                                 gamma_int = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_wood = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_fish = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_perm = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_area = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_PC = rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_PCinc= rnorm(1,0,10), gamma_SPinc = rnorm(1,0,10),
                                 p_int = rnorm(1,0,10), p_day1 = rnorm(1,0,10), p_day2 = rnorm(1,0,10), p_hour1 = rnorm(1,0,10), p_hour2 = rnorm(1,0,10))


# MCMC settings
ni <- 2000
nb <- ni*1/2
nt <- 1
nc <- 3


# Run the model
start.time <- Sys.time()
out2 <- nimbleMCMC(code = multiseason_nimble_car, constants = constants,
                  data = win.data, inits = initsFunction,
                  nchains = 3, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, thin = nt,
                  #summary = TRUE, # WAIC = TRUE,
                  monitors = params)
Sys.time()-start.time


# SUMMARY
parms<-c("psi1_int","psi1_fish","psi1_perm","psi1_area","psi1_wood",
         "phi_int","phi_fish","phi_PC","phi_perm","phi_area","phi_wood",
         "gamma_int","gamma_fish","gamma_PC","gamma_perm","gamma_area","gamma_wood","gamma_PCinc","gamma_SPinc",
         "p_int","p_day1","p_day2","p_hour1","p_hour2")


summary(out2$chain1[,colnames(out2$chain1)%in%parms])
summary(out2$chain2[,colnames(out2$chain2)%in%parms])
summary(out2$chain3[,colnames(out2$chain3)%in%parms])

messages.subject: Re: Dynamic occupancy model with spatial random effect (dcar_normal)
parts:
hi Mattia,

I don't have time to look in detail right now, but often this sort of thing is a problem of initial values. In particular you may want to initialize all sets of random effects that have the dcar_normal distribution at reasonable starting values. You probably don't need to have particularly "good" values, but simply have values that are not all zero (so that the model doesn't start out with a variance component tending to zero in the initial MCMC steps) and have variability consistent with any variance component that determines their variability. 

Do you have the problem when you use NIMBLE for the same model as you're able to fit in JAGS, or just for the expanded model(s)?

-Chris

messages.subject: Re: Dynamic occupancy model with spatial random effect (dcar_normal)
parts: I'll add that a good way to diagnose where the model is not initialized well, if that is the problem, is to build it outside of nimbleMCMC and calculate different parts of it.  For example, model$calculate("x") would return the sum of log probabilities of all nodes in the variable x.  If this is NA or -Inf, then x itself or something that x depends on may not be initialized well.

In particular you may want to initialize all sets of random effects that have the dcar_normal distribution at reasonable starting values. You probably don't need to have particularly "good" values, but simply have values that are not all zero (so that the model doesn't start out with a variance component tending to zero in the initial MCMC steps) and have variability consistent with any variance component that determines their variability.

I tried to set reasonable starting values for the variance of the dcar_normal distribution, with:
dunif("number of sites", 0, "some value")
I tried for example: 
psi1_rho=runif(202,0,100)
phi_rho=runif(202,0,100)
gamma_rho=runif(202,0,100)

The simpler model seems now to run fine, however nothing changed for the "full" model.
Having a deeper look into model initialization, I figured out that I forgot to insert a variable (fish) in constants.

I added the missing and ran the full model again, with the new initial values and not it seems to work!
Thank you very much!

Mattia

Il giorno mercoledì 18 dicembre 2019 01:41:39 UTC+1, pdevalpine ha scritto:

I'll add that a good way to diagnose where the model is not initialized well, if that is the problem, is to build it outside of nimbleMCMC and calculate different parts of it.  For example, model$calculate("x") would return the sum of log probabilities of all nodes in the variable x.  If this is NA or -Inf, then x itself or something that x depends on may not be initialized well.
